1987 
Gift from the Estate of Georgia O’Keeffe. Permanent loan from the New Mexico Museum of Art. 
(Source: UNM Art Museum, 2025)
remarks_1999: Museum files record lost inscription from verso: OK ☆ {star}  (unidentified hand, medium unknown); "One of O'Keeffe's best works in her personal collection" (probably Stieglitz, medium unknown). O'Keeffe wrote: "The Black Place is about one hundred and fifty miles from Ghost Ranch, and as you come to it over a hill, it looks like a mile of elephants—grey hills all about the same size with almost white sand at their feet" (Georgia O'Keeffe 1976, unpaginated, text accompanying entry 59). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: New Mexico Museum of Art, Santa Fe, Gift of the Estate of Georgia O'Keeffe, 1987
description: Tall, craggy gray hills with hints of red and yellow spread across the canvas. A few blue-gray bushes populate the flat land at the base of the hills. A small strip of clear blue sky is visible above the landscape.
